# `Email`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Email — provider-abstract email send.

Supports Resend, AWS SES, SendGrid, and raw SMTP under one API.

The provider is passed EXPLICITLY as the first argument to every send:
`Email.send provider message`. Provider configuration is intentionally NOT
part of the global `config` binding and is never ambient-installed — an
"install once, a later send reads it" path would admit a representable
"used-before-installed" state, which this API refuses to represent. A send
without a provider is a type error, not a runtime surprise.

Every provider credential is a `Secret` (`Ipe.Secret`): the Resend and
SendGrid API keys, the SES secret key, and the SMTP password are all sealed
and cannot be `Debug`-printed, stringified, logged, or serialised. The
runtime send kernel reveals each `Secret` only at the actual HTTP/SMTP call —
the plaintext never reaches a log line or an error message.

Every typed record ships with a `default*` constructor + `with*` builder
helpers so future field additions don't break record literals.

Example:

```ipe ipe:skip illustrative; wiring a provider, a message and the top-level send, not a standalone program
import Ipe.Secret

provider : EmailProvider
provider =
    Resend (Secret.fromString (System.getenvOr "RESEND_API_KEY" ""))

msg : EmailMessage
msg =
    case ( Email.parseAddress "noreply@example.com"
         , Email.parseAddress "alice@example.com"
         ) of
        ( Just from, Just to ) ->
            Email.defaultMessage { from = from, to = [ to ], subject = "Hi" }
                |> Email.withTextBody "Hello, world!"
        _ ->
            -- addresses above are compile-time constants and always parse;
            -- a real caller still has to cover this arm

main =
    Email.send provider msg
```

## `EmailMessage`

A single email message.

Build with `defaultMessage { from, to, subject }` + `with*`
helpers; never construct via record literal so future fields
don't break call sites.

Address fields (`from`, `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `replyTo`) require
`EmailAddress` values — constructed via `parseAddress`.  This makes
an invalid address a compile error rather than a runtime bounce.

## `Attachment`

A file attachment.  `content` carries the raw bytes as `Bytes`
(`Vec<u8>` on Rust).  Use `Bytes.fromString` for text content or
`File.readFileBytes` for binary files.

## `EmailProvider`

The provider to send through.  Pass explicitly to `send`.  The Resend and
SendGrid API keys are sealed `Secret`s; the SES / SMTP credentials live in
their config records (also sealed).

## `SesConfig`

SES auth: region + credentials.  The access-key id (`key`) identifies the
IAM principal and is not itself a secret (it travels in the request's
`Authorization` credential scope); the `secret` access key IS a credential
and is a sealed `Secret`.

## `SmtpConfig`

SMTP transport: host + port + creds.  The `pass` is a sealed `Secret`.

The `port` field is a raw `Int` because it is the kernel-transport
serialisation the runtime `Email_send` reads directly.  Do NOT set it via a
record literal — the validated entry point is `withSmtpPort`, which takes a
range-checked `Ipe.Net.Port` and unwraps it here, so an out-of-range port
cannot reach the transport.

## `defaultMessage`

```ipe
defaultMessage : { from : EmailAddress, to : List EmailAddress, subject : String } -> EmailMessage
```

Construct a baseline message with the three required fields
(`from`, `to`, `subject`).  Address fields take `EmailAddress`
values — use `parseAddress` to obtain them.  Optional address
fields default to empty; `replyTo` defaults to `from`.

## `defaultAttachment`

```ipe
defaultAttachment : String -> Attachment
```

`defaultAttachment "report.pdf"` — Attachment named with empty
mime type + empty byte content.  Pair with `withMimeType` + `withContent`
(or pass `File.readFileBytes` output directly to `withContent`).

## `withMimeType`

```ipe
withMimeType : String -> Attachment -> Attachment
```

`withMimeType "application/pdf" att` — replace the MIME type.

## `withContent`

```ipe
withContent : Bytes -> Attachment -> Attachment
```

`withContent bytes att` — replace the attachment body bytes.

## `defaultSesConfig`

```ipe
defaultSesConfig : String -> SesConfig
```

`defaultSesConfig "us-east-1"` — SesConfig with the region set;
pair with `withSesKey` + `withSesSecret` to provision credentials.  The
secret access key starts sealed-empty.

## `withSesKey`

```ipe
withSesKey : String -> SesConfig -> SesConfig
```

`withSesKey "AKIA..." cfg` — replace the SES access-key id (the IAM
principal identifier — not itself a secret).

## `withSesSecret`

```ipe
withSesSecret : Secret -> SesConfig -> SesConfig
```

`withSesSecret (Secret.fromString "...") cfg` — replace the SES secret
access key.  The value is a sealed `Secret`; it is revealed only at the send
kernel's SigV4 signing step, never logged.

## `defaultSmtpConfig`

```ipe
defaultSmtpConfig : String -> SmtpConfig
```

`defaultSmtpConfig "smtp.example.com"` — SmtpConfig with host
set, port 587 (submission), and empty credentials.  Most providers
expect SMTP submission on 587; override via `withSmtpPort` for 465
(implicit TLS) or 25 (legacy, no TLS).

## `withSmtpPort`

```ipe
withSmtpPort : Port -> SmtpConfig -> SmtpConfig
```

`withSmtpPort (Net.fromInt 465 |> Result.withDefault Net.min) cfg` — replace
the SMTP port with a range-validated `Ipe.Net.Port`.  An out-of-range port is
a construction-time `Err` on the `Net.fromInt` boundary, so it can never reach
this setter (and thus never the transport).

## `withSmtpUser`

```ipe
withSmtpUser : String -> SmtpConfig -> SmtpConfig
```

`withSmtpUser "user" cfg` — replace the SMTP username.

## `withSmtpPass`

```ipe
withSmtpPass : Secret -> SmtpConfig -> SmtpConfig
```

`withSmtpPass (Secret.fromString "...") cfg` — replace the SMTP password.
The value is a sealed `Secret`; it is revealed only at the send kernel's SMTP
AUTH step (over a required-TLS channel when credentials are set), never logged.

## `send`

```ipe
send : EmailProvider -> EmailMessage -> Task Error String
```

`send provider message` — submit the message to the chosen provider.
The provider is a REQUIRED positional argument (there is no default and no
ambient install), so a send is impossible without one.  Returns the
provider's message ID on success.  Fails on network errors, auth errors, or
invalid input (missing recipient, etc.).

The provider's sealed credentials cross into the runtime kernel still sealed;
the kernel reveals each `Secret` only at the outbound HTTP/SMTP call. No auth
error or diagnostic returned from a failed send carries the plaintext.

## `EmailAddress`

An opaque, validated email address.  Construct only via `parseAddress`.

## `parseAddress`

```ipe
parseAddress : String -> Maybe EmailAddress
```

Parse-don't-validate: attempt to parse a string as an RFC 5322 address.
Returns `Nothing` if the string is not a valid address; never silently accepts.

## `addressToString`

```ipe
addressToString : EmailAddress -> String
```

Render an `EmailAddress` back to its canonical string form.
